title: 01 · Disruption event
text: The flight has just been cancelled in the mock operations system. I have not touched the agent. I am publishing the native disruption event now. Its subscriber opens a real Salesforce Case for the synthetic passenger. Here is the independently queried Case and its event reference. This implementation does not yet send a proactive outbound message or refresh Data 360 from the event, so I am not claiming those steps. The Case is real; outbound delivery remains a release gate.

title: 02 · Deterministic identity
text: This passenger existed twice, with two email variants and one PNR. The live Data 360 query shows both source records linked to one unified profile. Fourteen source records resolve into thirteen profiles. The deployed rule requires exact canonical verified email, exact SkyMiles identifier, and exact surname together. It does not use a fuzzy name match. Here are the source links and the exact rule. Raw records and preprocessing lineage are retained, but native unmerge has not been demonstrated.

title: 03 · Grounded answer
text: The agent is answering from verified customer context and the live status call. The unified Data Graph verifies the passenger identity. Native Data 360 federation reads current loyalty context from Snowflake, with consent required in the query. The cancellation comes from the synthetic reservation service, with its source field and timestamp visible here. Contact data is masked in the context response, and payment data is never returned by this API. The text below is the actual published Agentforce response.

title: 04 · Live reservation options
text: Now watch the boundary. The agent is not inventing options. It is calling the external reservation system now, and this trace is that call. These two options came back from that system. Both are in the permitted cabin and within the pilot recovery window. Notice the inventory timestamp and the correlation identifier alongside the request. The Salesforce and Snowflake dependencies are real. The reservation system is our executable synthetic service. Live seat inventory remains there, rather than being copied into Data 360. No booking has been made yet.

title: 05 · Explicit acceptance and booking
text: The passenger picks the earlier flight. The agent records that exact selection and posts it back to the reservation system using a short-lived acceptance identifier and an idempotency key. The confirmation and booking reference you see came from that system, not from the agent. The successful transaction also synchronizes a real Salesforce Case. The Case number and synchronization result are shown alongside the authoritative reservation confirmation.

title: 06 · Trust boundary
text: Now I will try to push it past its limit. I am asking for a two hundred and fifty dollar voucher, above the two hundred dollar pilot threshold. It should refuse to do this alone, and it does. The API creates an approval proposal without issuing the voucher. The agent requests human review with the identity, loyalty, cancellation, booking, voucher and trace context attached to the Case. A Case update does not prove that a staffed queue or a human has received it; that distinction remains visible.

title: 07 · Inventory gone: HTTP 409
text: Last test. We are using a fresh, isolated reservation ledger. The seat has just gone, so the external system returns four oh nine, inventory gone. The trace shows the actual rejected rebooking request. The agent does not invent a seat. It re-queries, offers the next real option, and would escalate if none existed. No booking is created by this failed attempt.
